clue.text: One used whip on offspring endlessly

parts.note: the cat (o' nine tails) is a whip

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for offspring loses its final letter

parts.note: spawn is offspring, especially of fish or frogs

explanation.surface: Someone takes a whip to their children, apparently without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from SPAWN, leaving SPAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe manipulated by someone else, like the monkey's helper in the fable who pulled chestnuts from the fire, is a person used.

clue.text: Vehicle taking bird round city

indicators.note: round says the bird's name goes around the city's name

parts.note: a chat is a small songbird
Rio de Janeiro, commonly shortened to Rio, is a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A carriage carrying a bird around a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the city into the bird after its second letter rather than around its whole length.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used in ancient racing and war is a vehicle.

clue.text: Somehow unsound artistic work of the bard

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare play that is in some way unsound artistically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges UNSOUND ARTISTIC. 'The bard' is Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote this early revenge tragedy, so it is one of his plays.

clue.text: Way to engage people in physical exercise

definitions.text: Way to engage people in physical exercise

indicators.note: in says the road-and-people unit sits inside the abbreviation for exercise

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: to engage means to hold, so the word for way holds the word for people

parts.note: a road is a way
men are people

explanation.surface: A walkway designed to get folk taking exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to engage' and 'in' nest the pieces, and the whole clue doubles as the definition: a seafront walk gets people exercising.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront walkway is a path where people stroll for exercise.

clue.text: Decline to engage unknown actor

indicators.note: to engage means to take in, so the word for decline takes in the unknown

parts.note: to wane is to decline
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Refusing to hire a performer nobody has heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' suggests refusing; it means wane. John Wayne was a Hollywood star of westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wayne was a Hollywood film star, so he is an actor.

clue.text: Something of a habit round old London street

indicators.note: round says the headwear goes around the abbreviation for old

parts.note: a wimple is the head covering that forms part of a nun's habit

explanation.surface: A nun's garment is wrapped around some old street in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid as held reads WAMPOLE, but the wordplay builds WIMPOLE, the London street famous for doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimpole Street is a real thoroughfare in Marylebone, central London.

clue.text: They charged for washers or nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Someone billed for the washers or the nuts in a hardware order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like hardware next to 'washers'; it is the anagram signal. 'charged' means rushed at the enemy, not billed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry horses ridden into battle are animals that made charges.

clue.text: Middle East — general skirmish

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general leads a skirmish in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused hand-to-hand fight is a scuffle or brief clash.

clue.text: Acting superior, experiencing elation with heroin

parts.note: being on one's high means experiencing elation
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user feels superior while elated on heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: HORSE is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave arrogantly is to act as if raised above others, the idiom picturing a rider looking down.

clue.text: Old tennis player applied to football team

parts.note: Chris Evert was a leading tennis player of the 1970s and 80s
on means applied to, as a coat on a wall

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star has applied to a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is an English Premier League football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: Novelist wanting another plot only fretted

indicators.note: fretted means worried or agitated, so the letters of the three words are churned up

explanation.surface: A writer lacking a second storyline gets anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fretted' rearranges the fifteen letters of ANOTHER PLOT ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian author of the Barchester books was a prolific writer of fiction.

clue.text: Cause publication

explanation.definitionFit: A cause in dispute is the matter at issue, and a magazine number put out on a date is a publication.

clue.text: Making a bolt work placed in fire, say

indicators.note: placed in says the short word for work sits inside the longer word

parts.note: fire is one of the four classical elements, the say marking it as an example
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Building a door fastener and putting it in the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a bolt' looks like metalwork; to make a bolt is to run off, here to marry in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away secretly to marry is to make a bolt for it with a lover.

clue.text: Much defensive work in rugby, repelling thousand hangers-on

indicators.note: repelling means driving out, so the letter for thousand is pushed out of the phrase

parts.note: ten tackles is a lot of defensive effort in a rugby match

explanation.surface: A rugby team does lots of tackling while keeping out a thousand fans who cling on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelling' removes K (thousand) from TEN TACKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus's arms are things that grip and cling, so they are literally hangers-on.

clue.text: I bed endlessly in succession

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'I bed endlessly in succession', has no definition and no parse to LIBERTINE (LINE around BERTI suggests a garbled 'Bertie endlessly'); OCR damage beyond 3 letters

clue.text: Writer hot in head

indicators.note: in says the letter for hot goes inside the slang word for head

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An author feels feverish in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAN is old slang for the head. Brendan Behan was an Irish playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan Behan wrote Borstal Boy and The Quare Fellow, so he is an author.

clue.text: Thick book, quite dry

parts.note: rainless means without rain, quite dry

explanation.surface: A heavy volume about a very arid place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick book' reads as a fat volume; 'Thick' alone is the definition, meaning stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is slang for stupid, lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Succeeded in remedy for plague

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for succeeded sits inside the word for remedy

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Someone has found a treatment for the plague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plague' looks like a noun after 'remedy for'; it is the verb, to torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague someone is to afflict them, as a malediction is meant to.

clue.text: Man being driven stiff

indicators.note: being here means being in, so the man's name is placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is the thing that is driven
Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is being driven hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being driven' suggests being urged on; read as being inside the thing driven. 'stiff' looks like an adjective; it is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Cover with bright spots GP enables to be treated

indicators.note: treated as in handled or processed, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A family doctor lets a patient with a rash be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be treated' rearranges GP ENABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To spangle something is to deck it with glittering points, and the be- prefix makes it cover all over.

clue.text: Roman cavalry, one taken from stock

indicators.note: taken from says the letter for one is removed from the word for stock

parts.note: equities are company stock or shares
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One horseman is removed from the Roman cavalry's roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The equites were Rome's knightly order, originally its mounted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The equites were the Roman knights who originally served as mounted soldiers.

clue.text: Processes one used in bridge etc

indicators.note: used in says the letter for one is fitted inside the dental word

parts.note: a dental bridge is one kind of false teeth
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A procedure involving a card played at bridge and similar games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like the card game; here it is a dental bridge, so DENTURES.
explanation.definitionFit: To denature alcohol is to process it so it becomes undrinkable, so the word means treats or processes.

clue.text: Fish — pike is about right

indicators.note: is about says the charge word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: pike is short for turnpike, a road where a toll is paid

explanation.surface: A fish called a pike is said to be close to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pike' looks like the fish; here it is a turnpike, the toll.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat.

clue.text: Seafood: some gives us hiccups

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Raw fish gives some people hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese vinegared rice often served with raw fish, a sea dish.

clue.text: Former statesman turned chicken by Rugby

indicators.note: turned says the bird's word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
RU is short for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: An old politician became cowardly because of the rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes NEH from HEN. Nehru was India's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru led India from independence in 1947 until 1964, a politician now dead.

clue.text: Its output could lead to erotic arts and vices

definitions.text: Its output could lead to erotic arts and vices

indicators.note: the answer's letters, when output in a new order, could lead to the clue's words

explanation.surface: A lingerie firm's products might encourage sensual pastimes and sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words EROTIC ARTS VICES are an anagram of the answer, and the lingerie brand's products fit the suggestive reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria's Secret is an American lingerie retailer whose goods are designed to be alluring.

clue.text: Determine what to do with old crosswords

definitions.text: what to do with old crosswords

explanation.definitionFit: To settle on a course is to make a firm decision; doing a crossword again is to solve it once more.

clue.text: Staged parts of Oxford, say

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university city; it is a lace-up shoe, whose arches over the foot are the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in stages means done step by step; the arched tops of a shoe over the foot are its parts.
